source.title: Characterizing Inter-Layer Functional Mappings of Deep Learning Models
source.authors: D. Waagen; Katie Rainey; Jamie Gantert; David Gray; Megan King; M. S. Thompson; Jonathan Barton; Will Waldron; S. Livingston; D. Hulsey

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplement supplied; no evident truncation or garbling affecting the findings.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the random-label setting with a single CNN and layer-wise class-separation statistics, rather than directly reporting training and test error as the original sources do.
record.gate_note: The study reports results for CIFAR10 with randomly permuted labels. Its layer-separation analyses bear on V1 and V4, but it does not report classification training error, test error, epoch-to-fit timing, unstructured-input results, regularization comparisons, or a real-labels-first training trajectory. No study results test V2, V3, V5, or V6. Cited findings from Zhang et al. are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses random-label training to demonstrate a layer-analysis method. Its own results measure HP class-pair separation, not classification training error, test error, convergence time, or learning order. Near-complete separation on a 10,000-image training subset does not establish near-zero classification error on the full training set. These results therefore do not test V1 or V4 as defined.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present HP statistics as a way to identify memorizing layers, distance-preserving mappings, and training-validation discrepancies. They interpret random-label training separation as memorization, without reporting classification error rates that establish V1 or V4.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR10 with randomly permuted labels and a simple CNN trained with categorical cross entropy and SGD, but analyzes inter-layer class-separation statistics rather than directly measuring fit error and test error as in the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset label condition (random versus true) and the layer being analyzed; Euclidean and cosine distance analyses are reported as showing similar trends.

fits_no_version.finding: After 200 epochs of random-label training, dense layers produce training-subset HP statistics near one from an initially mixed state. The 5.ReLU-to-6.Dense increase is 0.750–0.758 across five models (Table 5). Validation data show no consistently significant layerwise separation improvement (Section 4.5; Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A CNN trained on randomly permuted CIFAR10 labels develops class-separated representations of sampled training examples in its dense layers without comparable separation of independently labeled validation examples.

record.problems: Only one simple CNN architecture is studied. Random-label results are capped at 200 epochs, and the study does not give classification training or test error for the random-label runs. The random-label classes are assessed with a 10,000-example analysis sample; the class-separation measure is indirect evidence for fitting.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: results relevant to the tested versions are class-separation statistics, not the training/test error measures named by the versions. The paper's narrative describes these separations, but no matching row-level measure is reported.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero classification training error on the full randomly labeled training set and chance test error under unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across a sweep of label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization; their omission alone provides no comparison.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels during training. Initialized-versus-final layer comparisons do not establish temporal learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly marks V1 and V4 as tested. Its rows_left_out already declares the omitted HP results, so they are not missing claim-testing rows. Differences between convolutional and dense layers describe where separation occurs, not when real labels and noise are learned.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures class-pair separation, not whether training classification error reaches zero or test error is at chance. It does state that the random-label dense layers separate training classes from a totally mixed state, but gives no classification error values.
Only the all-random CIFAR10 label condition is studied; no sweep of corrupted-label fractions or test-error trajectory is reported. Class separation is measured rather than training and test error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
